cards.title: The layer contract
items: View → ViewModel → SDK → Backend API: the View renders and forwards events, the ViewModel owns presentation state and commands, the SDK is a plain TypeScript client
the walls are lint rules, not suggestions — no-restricted-imports pins views (no SDK, no fetch, no token), viewmodels (no react-dom, react-native, chrome.*, router) and sdk (no React)
platform differences enter through ports: TokenStore, Transport and Clock for the SDK; Navigator, Notifier and Permissions for the ViewModel

cards.title: The delivery mechanism
items: three skills ship: react-best-practices loads on every React edit, react-review writes a prioritized report, react-port ports another framework with the tests first
lints/eslint.config.mjs is a copy-in ESLint 9 flat config; lints/check/ is the violation harness — one deliberate file per rule with a // expect:<rule> marker plus a clean control
scripts/check-lints.sh fails if a marked rule stays quiet, if anything unmarked fires, or if tsc --noEmit fails on the same files; CI runs it as the lints job

cards.title: State, errors and trust
items: one status union per screen — loading | empty | ready | forbidden | error — never three booleans that can contradict each other
the error envelope is { error: { code, message, requiredPermission?, correlationId } }; the SDK normalizes it into a typed union and the correlation id is copyable on the error screen
authorization is server-side: the UI hides an action with can("leads.delete"), the API rejects the request regardless of what the client renders

cards.title: What this repo is not
items: there is no runtime here: the skills are instructions and reference text only — no network calls, no data collected (PRIVACY.md)
there is no backend, no database and no queue in this repository; the Backend API is an external system the taught contract talks to
the package is a plugin: plugin.json carries the com.openai interface block, and scripts/package-openai-plugin.py ships it to Codex and ChatGPT
